title: LangChain and LangGraph Agent Frameworks Reach v1.0 Milestones
summary: LangChain released LangGraph 1.0 and LangChain 1.0 as stable versions on 22 October 2025. LangChain says LangGraph persists execution state automatically, so an agent interrupted by a server restart or a long-running pause resumes where it stopped, and workflows can be saved and resumed without custom database code. Human-in-the-loop pauses get first-class API support. The team commits to no breaking changes until 2.0; the main change is moving langgraph.prebuilt into langchain.agents.
relevance: A stable, widely used framework now treats checkpoint/resume as a core guarantee, which is the baseline mechanism for relocating a running agent task.
notes: The URL langchain.com/blog/langgraph-v1 from search actually serves the 2025-09-02 alpha post; this item uses the GA post.

title: LangGraph Platform is now Generally Available: Deploy & manage long-running, stateful Agents
summary: LangChain made LangGraph Platform generally available on 14 May 2025 as hosted infrastructure for long-running, stateful agents. The post describes a persistence layer for memory and conversation history, built-in checkpointing that lets developers rewind, edit and rerun a failed step, 30 API endpoints and horizontal scaling. LangChain says about 400 companies had deployed agents with it since the June 2024 beta. The product was later renamed LangSmith Deployment (October 2025).
relevance: Managed checkpoint stores with rewind and replay are the server-side substrate on which agent state can be suspended, inspected and resumed elsewhere.

title: Production-ready agents with the OpenAI Agents SDK + Temporal
summary: Temporal announced a durable-execution integration for the OpenAI Agents SDK, built with OpenAI and released as a Python public preview on 30 July 2025. The agent loop and handoffs run inside Temporal Workflows, and each agent or model invocation runs as a Temporal Activity, so retries, state and crash recovery come from Temporal. The integration works by supplying Temporal's own implementation of the SDK's abstract Runner class. A later update on the page says the Python integration became generally available on 23 March 2026.
relevance: It shows a third-party durable runtime wrapping another vendor's agent framework, so agent handoffs and state survive process failure without rewriting the agent.

title: AI agent reliability startup Temporal raises $300M in funding
summary: SiliconANGLE reported that Temporal closed a $300 million Series D led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Lightspeed and Sapphire Ventures, at a $5 billion valuation. The article says the open-source Temporal project is downloaded more than 20 million times a month and that Temporal Cloud can process over 300,000 AI agent actions per second (company claim). It names OpenAI and Nordstrom among customers and describes event-log-based resumption and cross-data-center failover.
relevance: Large investment explicitly framed around AI-agent reliability signals that durable state and failover are becoming standard infrastructure for agent execution.
search_query: Temporal raises Series funding AI agents 2025

title: Temporal Raises $550 Million Series E At $12.55 Billion Valuation As AI Infrastructure Demand Surges
summary: Temporal raised a $550 million Series E led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with Wellington, Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Tiger Global as co-leads, at a $12.55 billion valuation. The company says its annualized revenue run rate passed $250 million (up more than 200% year on year), Temporal Cloud processed over 1.9 trillion actions in August 2026, and open-source installations exceeded 43 million that month. Named customers include OpenAI, Snap, NVIDIA, Netflix and JPMorgan Chase.
relevance: Usage and revenue figures, though company-reported, give a dated measure of how fast durable execution is being adopted as agent infrastructure.

notes: GeekWire coverage of the same round returned HTTP 403, so the Pulse 2.0 article was used. The exact announcement date was not checked against a Temporal press release. The article gives both 'more than 4,300' and 'more than 4,000' customers.

title: Mem0 raises $24M from YC, Peak XV and Basis Set to build the memory layer for AI apps
summary: Mem0 announced $24 million in total funding: a previously undisclosed $3.9 million seed led by Kindred Ventures and a $20 million Series A led by Basis Set Ventures, with Peak XV, GitHub Fund and Y Combinator. TechCrunch reports over 41,000 GitHub stars, more than 13 million Python downloads, and API calls rising from 35 million in Q1 2025 to 186 million in Q3. Mem0 says it is the exclusive memory provider for AWS's Agent SDK, and the founder pitches a 'memory passport' that follows a user across apps and agents.
relevance: The 'memory passport' framing is an explicit commercial bet on model- and framework-independent memory, which is a form of portable agent context.
search_query: Mem0 Series A announcement TechCrunch October 2025 Basis Set

title: Managing context on the Claude Developer Platform
summary: Anthropic launched two public-beta features on 29 September 2025: context editing, which clears stale tool calls and results as the context window fills, and a memory tool that stores information as files in a directory whose backend the developer hosts. Anthropic reports that on an internal agentic-search evaluation, memory plus context editing improved performance by 39% over baseline and context editing alone by 29%, and that in a 100-turn web search test context editing cut token use by 84%. The features are also available on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI.
relevance: Putting agent memory in developer-controlled files outside the model makes the context store explicit and movable, which is a building block for a portable task envelope.
search_query: Anthropic "context management" memory tool Claude Developer Platform announcement
notes: anthropic.com/news/context-management redirects (308) to this claude.com URL.

title: Claude can now import chat histories from ChatGPT (and other AIs)
summary: PCWorld reported that Anthropic released an Import Memory tool so users can move context from ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot into Claude. The tool generates a prompt that the user runs in the old assistant, and the output is pasted into Claude's memory. The article says Claude needs about 24 hours to absorb the imported memories, and users can then review and edit them.
relevance: It is a dated, consumer-scale case of moving an assistant's accumulated user context between vendors, carried as model-generated text rather than a structured format.
search_query: Claude import memory from ChatGPT announcement
notes: The article was translated from PC för Alla (Swedish). Anthropic's own announcement was not located; the tool lives at claude.com/import-memory, which is a product page rather than a dated news item.

title: Make the switch: Bring your AI memories and chat history to Gemini
summary: Google launched two Gemini import tools on 26 March 2026. With memory import, the user runs a Gemini-supplied prompt in another AI app and pastes the resulting summary into Gemini. With chat history import, the user uploads a ZIP export from another provider, then searches and continues those conversations in Gemini. Google also renamed 'past chats' to 'memory'. The tools exclude Business, Enterprise and under-18 accounts and are not yet available in the EEA, UK or Switzerland.
relevance: Together with Claude's import tool, it shows major vendors converging on cross-assistant context transfer, using prompt-generated summaries and raw export archives instead of a shared schema.
search_query: blog.google Gemini "import" memory chat history switching from other AI apps March 2026
notes: PCWorld secondary coverage (2026-03-27, article 3100804) was not added separately.

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available
summary: AWS made Amazon Bedrock AgentCore generally available on 13 October 2025 as a framework- and model-agnostic platform for building and running agents. At GA, AgentCore Memory added a self-managed strategy that lets customers run their own memory extraction and consolidation pipelines. AgentCore Runtime keeps eight-hour execution windows with full session isolation and adds Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol support. All services gained VPC, PrivateLink, CloudFormation and tagging support across nine regions.
relevance: A hyperscaler bundles managed memory, isolated long-running sessions and A2A in one runtime, which defines the hosting surface that agent state must move into and out of.
search_query: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory generally available

title: Announcing Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank available for everyone in preview
summary: Google Cloud released Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank in public preview, a managed long-term memory service for agents. Gemini models asynchronously extract facts and preferences from Agent Engine Sessions, consolidate them with existing memories (resolving contradictions), and serve them by scope or similarity search. Memory Bank works natively with the Agent Development Kit and can be called from LangGraph and CrewAI. Google says the approach builds on a Google Research method accepted at ACL 2025 (arXiv:2503.08026).
relevance: A managed memory service that several frameworks can call separates user context from any single agent runtime, which is a precondition for moving tasks between frameworks.
search_query: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank announcement Google Cloud blog
notes: The page gave a publication date of 9 July 2025; the search-result summary said 8 July 2025. The fetched value is used.

title: Project Think: building the next generation of AI agents on Cloudflare
summary: Cloudflare previewed the next Agents SDK, which adds primitives for long-running agents on Durable Objects. runFiber() registers a durable invocation in SQLite before it runs, ctx.stash() saves a checkpoint so an evicted agent resumes from its last stash, and an experimental Session API stores conversations as forkable trees with non-destructive compaction. Sub-agents run as colocated child Durable Objects (Facets), each with an isolated SQLite database, and talk to the parent over typed RPC.
relevance: It turns checkpoint-on-eviction and parent/child sub-agents into edge-platform primitives, which directly concerns runtime relocation and delegation within one host.
search_query: Cloudflare Agents SDK Durable Objects announcement blog
notes: datePublished is 2026-04-15 and dateModified is 2026-07-15. Author attribution comes from the page's author section.

title: AWS Lambda announces durable functions for multi-step applications and AI workflows
summary: At re:Invent on 2 December 2025, AWS launched Lambda durable functions, which add 'steps' and 'waits' to the Lambda programming model to checkpoint progress and pause execution. AWS says workflows can pause for up to one year without compute charges and recover from failures without custom state code. At launch the feature was available in US East (Ohio) for Python 3.13/3.14 and Node.js 22/24.
relevance: Checkpoint-and-replay built into a mainstream serverless runtime makes durable, suspendable agent steps available without a separate orchestration engine.
search_query: AWS Lambda durable functions re:Invent 2025 announcement

title: Open source Workflow Development Kit is now in public beta
summary: Vercel released its open-source Workflow Development Kit in public beta. A 'use workflow' directive makes an async JavaScript function durable and 'use step' marks retryable steps, so agents can suspend, resume and keep state without queues or schedulers. sleep pauses a run without holding compute. Built-in traces, logs and metrics support replay and time-travel debugging, and workflows can be deployed to Vercel or other clouds.
relevance: A portable, cloud-neutral durable-execution layer for TypeScript agents expands where checkpointed agent runs can execute and be replayed.
search_query: Vercel Workflow Development Kit launch durable agents
notes: This is the official Vercel Community announcement post; Vercel's changelog entry was not fetched.

title: Agent File
summary: Letta introduced Agent File (.af), an open file format that serializes a stateful agent, including tool definitions, execution environment, model configuration and in-context and external memories, so it can be recreated on another server. Letta calls it the first file format for portable, reproducible agent state and says it enables moving agents between cloud and local servers, sharing and versioning them. Example .af agents and generation scripts are published in a GitHub repository.
relevance: It is a concrete serialization of full agent state for moving agents between hosts, and the closest existing analogue to a portable agent envelope.
search_query: Letta Agent File .af open format serialize stateful agents announcement
notes: The 'first file format' wording is Letta's claim. Per Letta's docs, the format applies to Letta servers, and secrets are nulled on export.

title: Berlin-based Restate raises $20M
summary: Restate, a Berlin-founded durable-execution startup, raised a $20 million Series A led by Singular, with Redpoint Ventures and Capital One Ventures, for $27 million in total funding. The money will fund product development and a San Francisco commercial hub. Restate, founded in 2024 by Apache Flink creators including CEO Stephan Ewen, says hundreds of organizations use its software to make AI agents and backends recover from crashes.
relevance: A second, independently funded durable-execution vendor positioned for agents shows competition forming around the runtime layer that agent checkpoint/resume depends on.
search_query: Restate raises funding durable AI agents OR Inngest raises Series agents 2025

title: Building Durable Agents with DBOS and Databricks
summary: On 7 April 2026 DBOS announced a technology partnership with Databricks and published a guide to running durable agents on Databricks Lakebase (serverless Postgres). DBOS checkpoints each LLM and tool call to the database, so an agent resumes from its last completed step after a crash. Workflows can be forked from a chosen checkpoint to test a fix without rerunning earlier expensive steps. The demo wraps an OpenAI Agents SDK agent as a DBOS workflow deployed as a Databricks app.
relevance: Postgres-resident checkpoints that can be forked show agent execution state treated as ordinary, portable database records.
search_query: DBOS Databricks partnership Lakebase durable agents press release
notes: The blog post links to a PR Newswire release of the same date (syndicated copies found via search); the release itself was not fetched.

title: ChatGPT Gets Total Recall: OpenAI's Memory Upgrade Remembers Your Whole Chat History
summary: Decrypt reported that on 10 April 2025 OpenAI upgraded ChatGPT memory so it can reference a user's entire past chat history, in addition to explicit saved memories. The rollout started with Pro, then Plus, with Team, Enterprise and Edu to follow, and excluded the EEA, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein. According to an OpenAI email cited in the article, chat-history references are not stored or shown in settings the way saved memories are, and OpenAI did not say how long history is retained.
relevance: Implicit, non-inspectable memory derived from chat history makes it harder to export and port user context, which the 2026 import tools later had to work around.
search_query: OpenAI ChatGPT memory references all past chats announcement April 2025
notes: OpenAI's primary page (openai.com/index/memory-and-new-controls-for-chatgpt/) returned HTTP 403, so secondary coverage was used.
